candidate.answerReason: Six copies of 6 to the sixth power sum to 6 times 6 to the sixth power, which is 6 to the seventh power.

methods.label: Turn repeated addition into multiplication
methods.explanation:
There are six identical addends \(6^6\), so their sum is \(6\cdot6^6\). Multiplication of powers with the same base adds the exponents:
\[
6\cdot6^6=6^1\cdot6^6=6^{1+6}=6^7.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{6^7}\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: Only repeated addition and the positive-integer exponent product rule are needed.
